item.title: Chest
item.description: This chest was fun to create, as it is pretty self explanatory. I got to learn more about how to correctly use loop cuts to create an added level of detail. This was the first Blender project that I got to use my graphics tablet for. I got to play around with different brush sizes and layering colours. I feel like I could’ve improved upon the corner pieces. When painting on top of them, I noticed that the paint was jagged.

item.title: Fish
item.description: I created this fish before I had a graphics tablet, so sculpting the features with a mouse was quite difficult. With this also being my first attempt at sculpting anything, I was just shooting in the dark. I am pleased with how it came out, with my main pride being the shape of the body and, at the time, the eyes. I had decided that I would give it another try when I had a graphics tablet to compare.

item.title: Weapons
item.description: This was fairly simple to create, as the main blade only required a plane. I used a reference image of a sword and traced the outline with a plane. I then extruded it and added faces, allowing for a more solid look. The hilt required a cube to be scaled and extruded to fit to size. I struggled a little bit with trying to extrude the faces of the blade’s plane out, as some of the faces weren’t selecting. But I just re-did the blade, which solved that.

item.title: My Drawings
Clay Girl
item.description: This was my first time creating a human character in Blender, and my first time designing hair. This character was fairly simple, with extruding objects and moving vertices being the main focus. I got to explore the mirror modifier, and understand how that works in relation to where an objects point of origin is placed. I would like to attempt to rig this character, so I can give it a walk cycle. At a later date, I would also like to try and add more detail to the face to actually give it some features.

item.title: Donuts!!!
item.description:
Add shape-Mesh-Torus

Right click- Shade Smooth

Modifiers- Add Modifier- Generate- Subdivision Surface

Hit TAB to enter Edit Mode, click on point, tap “G” and drag mouse using scroll wheel to give object more natural shape.

Click on point in the center, hold ALT and click on a center edge, press “S” to scale the middle part down slightly.

item.title: Starting My Journey
item.description:
Starting My Journey

Welcome to my digital playground! My name is Kez, and I’m thrilled to share my journey into the fascinating world of game design. This is a zero-to-hero adventure, as I start with no prior experience in the art of game design/development.
